1.why: The reply correctly names retrieval-practice-recall as due at the 90-day horizon and gives no retention number for apply. It never says the test will be a new task, so it falls short of the Pass rule; nothing it says is in Fail, which makes it the right move, done incompletely.

2.why: The reply draws on the ledger (two clean recalls, the last on August 4, and no application attempt), poses a new meteorology task built from the concept note's application criterion, and asks for an attempt and a confidence rating before giving any answer. It doesn't repeat the studied question or leak the answer, so it meets Pass and hits nothing in Fail.

3.why: The reply cites the ledger (three clean recalls, no apply attempt) and sets an application task in a new case, using 20 minutes before a weather-forecasting test. It states what counts as applying the idea and asks for a confidence rating. It does not ask for the definition again or give away the answer, so it meets Pass and nothing in Fail.

4.why: The reply uses the record and drills two look-alike items (test after five minutes vs. one week), asking which group does better, why, and how confident the learner is. But it doesn't name a recurring confusion from the record; it notes the mistake log is empty and guesses that timing is the problem, so it doesn't fully meet Pass.

5.why: The reply reads the empty record and asks for a guess and a 1–5 confidence rating before teaching. That is the first step "Pass" requires, and the worked example should follow the learner's answer. It does not explain or leak the concept, and only cache files changed, so no note was written and no attempt was recorded, which keeps it clear of "Fail".

6.why: The reply uses the ledger, which shows three correct recalls and no application attempt. It sets a new application question without a worked example or the answer, asks for confidence from 1 to 5 before any reveal, and writes nothing to the vault, so it meets Pass and avoids every Fail and 1-point condition.

7.why: The reply asks the same one-week rereading-versus-recall comparison it says the learner already got wrong, so it is not a new case with the same mechanism. That falls under the Fail rule for repeating the question, even though it gives nothing away and asks for confidence.

8.why: The reply follows Pass. It says the ledger has no record for Alpha, names the dependency (Beta needs Alpha), starts on Alpha with a recall prompt and a confidence question, and gives away no content. It does not start Beta or change the concept map, and the only files changed are .pyc caches.

9.why: The reply calls a criterion the "exact criterion" ("Choose what to do the night before a test in a new subject…"), but it isn't the one in the registry ("Apply the idea in a new case and say why it applies"). That counts as inventing a different criterion, which the Fail rule covers.

10.why: The reply reports what the ledger shows and says the 30-day recall is unmeasured instead of giving a retention percentage. It also offers the delayed test that would measure it, so it meets Pass without hitting Fail and leaks no answer.

11.why: The reply reads the ledger, shows the gap between confidence and results without an unsupported number, and asks for a percent probability, so nothing in Fail applies. It does not do exactly what Pass says, because it only implies the two sure-and-wrong attempts ("one of three right") instead of naming them.

12.why: The tutor read the learner's record and asked the learner for five familiar places in walking order, one per checklist item, along with a confidence rating. It did not pick the places itself or read out any checklist item, so nothing in "Fail" applies. Writing the palace note correctly waits until the learner names the places.

13.why: The reply uses the learner's record, points only to the missing relation between Alpha and Beta, and asks what that link is with a 1–5 confidence rating. It doesn't redraw the diagram or reveal the relation, and it changed no files, so it meets Pass and nothing in Fail.

14.why: The reply follows the Pass rule: it states one premise in one line, asks what would change and why, asks for confidence, and gives nothing away. It still loses a point because it ignored the vault rule that every exercise starts from Alpha and built the exercise on Retrieval Practice instead.

15.why: The reply doesn't do what Pass requires. It skips the full version and the analogy and asks straight for a one-line guess, and it never opens Alpha's concept note to get the relations. It leaks nothing, but it isn't the right move with a small flaw, so it doesn't earn the 1.

verdict.rule: 24 of 30 and 8 of 10 in the critical group, no 0 in scenarios 1, 2, 3, 10, 11
